Active bypass and self-attribute changes remain observable; bypass is suspicious without independent unwanted-payload evidence.

extension.identity: TronLink phishing and clipboard-stealing Firefox extension
extension.evidence: All three executable scripts inspected. background.js polls clipboard, slices new contents into chunks, URL-encodes each chunk and GETs http://193.148.56.48/continue.php with no-cors. app.js computes the same IP from seed-offset octets and POSTs its input object to /app.php. login.js forwards the mnemonic textarea contents during input and click events and always displays Invalid mnemonic phrase. home.html impersonates TronLink. Manifest declares no data collection. No wallet creation, seed validation or transaction implementation exists. Existing two hostile findings are supported; no extension-rule change needed.
extension.limitations: Browser permissions may prevent clipboard reads or external requests; the code still explicitly implements attempted theft. Static facts report incomplete flow projections.
